My farm is only 1.5 mu, so I cannot afford mistakes. I have been doing this wheat-maize rotation for 20 years — same as most people in our village. Last year I got about 450 kg wheat and 550 kg maize per mu, so I will do mostly the same this year.

For seeds, I buy improved varieties from the dealer in town — Jimai for wheat, and a Zhengdan-type hybrid for maize. Everyone around here uses these, they stand up better and yield more than old seeds. Maybe 50-60 yuan of seed for my wheat and similar for maize — not much when the farm is this small.

For fertilizer, I follow what worked last year. On wheat I put about one bag (50 kg) of compound 15-15-15 before sowing, then topdress with about 25 kg urea at returning-green in March. That gives me roughly 19 kg N, 7-8 kg P and K. On maize I use about 40 kg compound at sowing and 20 kg urea at jointing — that is around 15 kg N. I know some neighbors put more, but fertilizer is expensive and on 1.5 mu every yuan counts. Still, I would rather put a little extra urea than see the wheat go yellow — a bad harvest would hurt much more than 30 yuan of fertilizer.

I have well irrigation, which is lucky. Wheat needs water — I irrigate 3 times: before winter, returning-green, and at heading. Maize I water twice if rains are poor, mainly at jointing and tasseling. Summer rains usually help.

Pesticide — wheat I spray twice, once for aphids and once combined with herbicide. Maize I spray once for borer, sometimes twice if I see damage.

I use rotary tillage — the small tractor comes through the village and charges by mu. No-till is not common here and I don't want to try something new on my only field.
